A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same feature-averaging study. Their text, equations, figures and appendices support reliable comparison, including matching relocated proofs and experiments.

before.justification: V1 reports original synthetic simulations, feature-correlation analyses and adversarial-robustness experiments on MNIST and CIFAR-10, including appendix ablations.

after.justification: V2 retains original empirical results and adds unequal-norm synthetic experiments, adversarial-training comparisons, ResNet feature analyses and ℓ∞ robustness evaluations.

M1.justification: The formal models and training objectives remain unchanged. However, experimental binary prediction changes from aggregating class probabilities in v1 Section 6.2 to aggregating logits in v2 Section 5.2. This revises the reported inference procedure, although v2 Section 4.2 retains the probability-based definition.

E1.justification: The datasets remain synthetic clusters, MNIST and CIFAR-10. V2 changes MNIST binary classification from first-five versus last-five classes to parity classification, adds unequal-norm synthetic conditions, and extends evaluation to ℓ∞ perturbations.

E2.justification: V2 Appendix B.2 and Figure 11 add PGD adversarial training as a comparator to binary-label and fine-grained-label training on synthetic data. Training radii 20 and 40 are evaluated. This comparator was absent from v1's reported comparisons.

E3.justification: V2 adds a frozen, pretrained ResNet18 feature-extractor experiment and changes the retained CLIP experiment's reported head width from 30 to 1000. New protocols include adversarial training with m = 50 and radii 20/40, plus ℓ∞ PGD evaluation. These substantially revise experimental settings; the PDFs do not establish that retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: V1's sample-count, learning-rate, initialization, SNR and near-orthogonality studies are retained. V2 substantially broadens robustness analysis through unequal-norm sensitivity testing, investigation of feature decoupling under adversarial training, and testing fine-grained supervision under ℓ∞ attacks (Figures 10, 11 and 14).

E5.justification: Neither version reports empirical repeated-run counts, random seeds, error bars, confidence intervals or significance tests. The added experiments retain the existing curve and heatmap reporting practice.

E6.justification: V2 adds ResNet feature-correlation results, feature averaging under unequal norms, adversarial-training comparisons and ℓ∞ robustness curves (Figures 2, 10, 11 and 14). The latter comparisons favor fine-grained supervision. V1's CLIP heatmaps reappear in Figure 13, and Figure 3's ℓ2 curves are unchanged; these retained displays are not new performance gains.

T1.justification: The assumptions, Theorems 4.5–4.7, Proposition 4.8 and detailed proofs retain their mathematical substance. The proof sketch and appendices are relocated and renumbered; v2 Theorem C.2 simply restates Theorem 4.5.

C1.justification: Both versions claim that gradient descent learns feature averages that cause non-robustness, while fine-grained supervision enables feature decoupling and optimal robustness in the analyzed setting. The abstract, contribution list and conclusion preserve these claims and their scope.

C2.justification: V2 interprets the unequal-norm experiment as evidence that exact equinorm conditions can be relaxed empirically. Appendix B.2 also explains that adversarial training encourages feature decoupling, but less completely than fine-grained supervision. These supplement the retained mechanism explanation.

D1.justification: V2 documents settings for its added experiments but omits v1 Section 6.2's ResNet optimizer, batch size, momentum, weight decay, learning-rate schedules and epoch budgets. Appendix H.1 also specifies a 1000-neuron CLIP head with h = 10, which is inconsistent with its ten-group architecture.

R1.justification: V2 substantially expands research positioning through discussions of frequency bias (Xu et al., 2019/2024), CLIP neuron superposition (Gandelsman et al., 2024), and fine-grained part annotations (Sitawarin et al., 2022; Li et al., 2024). It also adds robust-feature and neural-collapse references, while removing Gu et al. (2024).

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction and experimental descriptions are extensively rewritten. V1 Section 5's proof overview moves to Appendix C, Section 7's conceptual discussion moves to Appendix A, and experimental appendices are reorganized into synthetic and real-world sections.

P2.justification: V2 adopts the ICLR layout throughout and reorganizes substantial visual material. Figure 2 gains ResNet panels, its original CLIP panels become Figure 13, and the old correlation Figure 10 becomes Figure 12. New Figures 10, 11 and 14 display unequal-norm, adversarial-training and ℓ∞ experiments.

improvement.justification: V2 strengthens empirical support through unequal-norm checks, an adversarial-training comparator and ℓ∞ evaluation, while preserving the central theory and improving research context. These gains are tempered by removed ResNet training details, inconsistent CLIP width documentation, and changed settings accompanying retained plots. The net improvement is useful but limited.
